---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

Write a script that accepts a version number through a placeholder and updates the code files (ex package.json, depends on coding language) so that the new version number is applied. Ex: if there is a package.json, update the version field.

New feature required in actions: ask user for info. Currently, only version number supported, which is predefined. Once the user has given this info, it can be reused for the release function.

So in action def, new select, currently only value\=version.

When such action is started, the frontend shows the dialog first. So backend asks frontend for value and waits for response before starting rest of action.

This can be for both command and agent actions.

Yes. I understand the feature as: an action can declare that it needs a `version`; when the action starts, the desktop backend requests that value from the frontend and waits. The value then resolves `{{version}}` in command text or agent prompts, including linked release actions. A project-specific script uses the supplied version to update files such as `package.json`.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add an optional input selector to action definitions, initially allowing only `version`. Update the shared types, validation, editor select, and serialization. Existing actions need no input.
2. Add a run input request and response over the Electron bridge. The runner should pause **before `onBefore` or the main action**, show a version dialog, and resume only after a valid value arrives. Cancelling the dialog cancels the run; closing the window or stopping the run must also clear the pending request.
3. Store the answer on the run, not on the card. Pass it through `onBefore`, `on`, and `onAfter` actions so the release action can reuse the same value without asking again. Validate a required value before executing anything.
4. Resolve `{{version}}` in both command and agent paths. This includes the editable agent prompt, which currently overrides the definition prompt, and the frontend prompt preview. Check all callers of the shared placeholder resolver before changing its inputs.
5. Define how unattended runs behave. Scheduled and state-triggered actions have no dialog; I would reject a run requiring `version` before it executes unless a value is explicitly supplied.
6. Add focused tests for definition validation, bridge request and response, cancellation, both executor types, linked-action reuse, and unattended runs. Update the action and placeholder documentation; run targeted tests and lint.

The script that edits version files should be **project-specific**: the description gives `package.json` as an example but does not define which languages or files a universal script must support. I would supply an example command action and script for the chosen project files once those targets are specified.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

# Placeholders

{% raw %}

Placeholders let one action definition work for every card. They are written as `{{name}}` and resolved on the desktop side, just before the process starts.

| Placeholder | Resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| `{{card-file}}` | Path to the selected card's Markdown file. |
| `{{this-card}}` | Alias of `{{card-file}}`; the same path to the selected card's Markdown file. |
| `{{card-title}}` | Title of the selected card. |
| `{{card-prompt}}` | The extra text you typed in the action popup for this run. |
| `{{active-cards-folder}}` | Absolute path to the configured working folder under the opened repository. Active cards are root-level Markdown files in this folder shown on the dashboard. |
| `{{worktree-folder}}` | Absolute path to the action execution checkout. |
| `{{repository-folder}}` | Absolute path to the opened repository. |
| `{{project-folder}}` | Absolute path to the configured `project.projectFolder` under the opened repository. Equal to `{{repository-folder}}` when configuration is empty. |
| `{{releases-folder}}` | Absolute path to the configured releases folder under the opened repository. |
| `{{diagram-file}}` | Output path for a diagram action. Available when the action has diagram output. |
| `{{parent-node}}` | Label of the selected item when running a child diagram action. |
| `{{diagram-changes}}` | Generated text from reviewed diagram edits when sending changes to an agent. |

They work in both `prompt` (agent actions) and `command` (command actions).

## Using them

In the prompt editor, type `{{` for a typeahead list, or insert one from the toolbar.

```json
{
  "id": "fix-bug",
  "label": "Fix bug",
  "description": "Fix the bug described on the card",
  "type": "agent",
  "prompt": "Fix the bug described in {{card-file}}.\n\nExtra instructions: {{card-prompt}}"
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "open-in-editor",
  "label": "Open in VS Code",
  "description": "Open the card file in VS Code",
  "type": "command",
  "command": "code {{card-file}}"
}
```

## Notes

- A card placeholder only resolves when the action runs with card context. Use `appliesTo` with `"kind": "card"` so an action that needs `{{card-file}}` or `{{this-card}}` is only offered where it makes sense.
- Diagram placeholders need diagram context. `{{diagram-file}}` also needs an output path, `{{parent-node}}` needs a selected item in a child diagram context, and `{{diagram-changes}}` needs reviewed changes from the editor.
- `{{card-prompt}}` is empty when you run without typing anything. Write prompts that read fine either way.
- During linked-worktree actions, `{{repository-folder}}`, `{{project-folder}}`, and `{{active-cards-folder}}` remain under the opened repository. Only `{{worktree-folder}}` changes to the linked worktree.
- The diff command in project configuration supports the same five folder placeholders plus `{{commit}}`, `{{branch}}`, and `{{file}}`. For diffs, `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{repository-folder}}` both resolve to the opened repository.
- Custom agent profiles support `{{model}}` in `command` and `{{sessionId}}` in `resumeCommand`. Those are profile placeholders, not action placeholders.

{% endraw %}

See also: [Action definition](action-definition.md), [Diagrams](../guide/diagrams.md), [Cookbook](cookbook.md).

export interface ActionPlaceholder {
    description: string
    name: 'active-cards-folder' | 'card-file' | 'card-prompt' | 'card-title' | 'diagram-changes' | 'diagram-file' | 'parent-node' | 'project-folder' | 'releases-folder' | 'repository-folder' | 'this-card' | 'worktree-folder'
}

export const ACTION_PROMPT_PLACEHOLDERS: readonly ActionPlaceholder[] = [
    { description: 'Absolute path to the folder containing root-level Markdown cards shown on the dashboard.', name: 'active-cards-folder' },
    { description: 'Path to the selected Markdown card file.', name: 'card-file' },
    { description: 'Alias of {{card-file}} with the same selected Markdown card file path.', name: 'this-card' },
    { description: 'Title of the selected card.', name: 'card-title' },
    { description: 'Additional prompt entered when the card action runs.', name: 'card-prompt' },
    { description: 'Reviewed change instructions captured from the active diagram edit session.', name: 'diagram-changes' },
    { description: 'Absolute path where the current diagram action must save its JSON output.', name: 'diagram-file' },
    { description: 'Label of the selected parent diagram item for a child diagram action.', name: 'parent-node' },
    { description: 'Absolute path to the configured project folder.', name: 'project-folder' },
    { description: 'Absolute path to the configured releases folder.', name: 'releases-folder' },
    { description: 'Absolute path to the opened repository.', name: 'repository-folder' },
    { description: 'Absolute path to the action run checkout.', name: 'worktree-folder' },
]

/** Format an action placeholder for insertion into template text. */
export function formatActionPlaceholder(name: ActionPlaceholder['name']) {
    return `{{${name}}}`
}

entries.content:
# Action definition

One JSON file per action, stored in the project's actions folder. Edit them through the action editor (tree â†’ action, or **New action** in the menu) â€” mdÂ² never shows raw JSON, but this is what ends up on disk.

{% raw %}
```json
{
  "id": "implement",
  "label": "Implement",
  "description": "Implement this feature",
  "type": "agent",
  "prompt": "Read and implement the feature described in {{card-file}}",
  "needsWorkTree": true,
  "appliesTo": { "kind": "card", "type": "feature" },
  "onBefore": ["prep-to-implement"],
  "onAfter": ["complete-card"]
}
```
{% endraw %}

## Fields

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | yes | Stable identifier. Links and run requests use it, so renaming the label never breaks a chain. Must be unique, also after normalization (`My Action` and `my_action` collide). |
| `label` | yes | Text shown on buttons and menu entries. |
| `description` | yes | Shown in the action popup. |
| `type` | yes | `agent` or `command`. |
| `prompt` | agent only | Markdown prompt. Not allowed on command actions. |
| `command` | command only | Command line. Not allowed on agent actions. |
| `icon` | no | Icon shown by entry points. |
| `appliesTo` | no | Filters deciding where the action appears. See below. |
| `output` | no | `{ "kind": "diagram" }` makes the action create a diagram. Requires `appliesTo.kind` to be `diagram`. |
| `onBefore` | no | Ordered list of action ids to run first. |
| `on` | no | Ordered list of `{ "condition": "<regex>", "actionId": "<id>" }` rules matched against this action's output. |
| `onAfter` | no | Ordered list of action ids to run afterwards. |
| `onState` | no | Card state that triggers this action when a card enters it. |
| `needsWorkTree` | no | When true, the action requires a card with a valid worktree assignment and runs there. |
| `trackFileChanges` | no | Agent actions only. Records the files the run touched. |
| `streaming` | no | Agent actions only. `true` keeps one live provider session across turns. |
| `autoFinish` | no | Agent actions only, requires `streaming`. `{ "state": "<card state>" }` finishes when a card reaches that state. Diagram-output actions can use `{ "when": "diagram-created" }` to finish when the diagram is created. |
| `agent` | no | Agent profile override. Required when `model` is set. |
| `model` | no | Model override. Requires `agent`. |
| `thinkingLevel` | no | `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `max`. Requires `agent` and `model`. |
| `phrases` | no | Named snippets (`title` + `text`) offered as quick buttons while running the action. |

Unknown fields are rejected at load time rather than silently ignored.

## `appliesTo`

An object of context filters. Every configured filter must match for the action to appear.

| Filter | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | Context type, for example `card`, `diagram`, `file`, `folder`. |
| `type` | Card type, for example `feature`, `bug`. |
| `state` | Card status. |
| `file` | File the context points at. |
| `folder` | Folder the context points at. |
| `worktree` | Worktree assignment on the card. |
| `worktreeError` | Worktree problem reported for the card. |

No `appliesTo` means the action is available in every supported context.

```json
"appliesTo": { "kind": "card", "state": "ready for implementation" }
```

## Diagram actions

Use `appliesTo.kind: "diagram"` and `output.kind: "diagram"` for an action that creates a diagram. Set `appliesTo.type` to `root` for a project-level diagram or `child` for a diagram opened from a selected item. In the action editor, choose **Diagram** as the output kind. The generated diagram is JSON at the path supplied by {% raw %}`{{diagram-file}}`{% endraw %}; agent prompts also receive the configured diagram footer. Streaming agent actions can finish automatically with `autoFinish: { "when": "diagram-created" }`.

{% raw %}
```json
{
  "id": "project-architecture",
  "label": "Project architecture",
  "description": "Generate an architecture diagram for this project",
  "type": "agent",
  "prompt": "Describe the main components and their connections.",
  "appliesTo": { "kind": "diagram", "type": "root" },
  "output": { "kind": "diagram" }
}
```
{% endraw %}

See [Diagrams](../guide/diagrams.md) for the editing workflow and [Placeholders](placeholders.md) for diagram-specific placeholders.

## Validation

Definitions are validated when they load and again before they are saved. mdÂ² refuses to run or store an action that fails, and shows the error on the offending field. Rejected cases include:

- missing `id`, `label`, `description`, or `type`;
- duplicate or normalization-colliding ids;
- `prompt` on a command action, `command` on an agent action;
- `streaming`, `autoFinish`, or `trackFileChanges` on a command action;
- `autoFinish` without `streaming`, or an `autoFinish.state` that is not a configured column;
- diagram output without diagram applicability, or a `diagram-created` auto-finish trigger without diagram output;
- `model` without `agent`, `thinkingLevel` without both;
- an unknown agent profile or a model the profile does not list;
- an invalid regular expression in an `on` condition;
- an unknown action id in `onBefore`, `on`, or `onAfter`;
- a cycle through `onBefore`, `on`, or `onAfter`;
- unknown fields, and the retired fields `after`, `before`, `runIn`, `text`, or type `cmd`.

## Built-in actions

Two actions exist without a file:

| Id | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `md2.custom-prompt` | Sends whatever you type to the agent. Streaming. Always available in supported contexts. |
| `md2.convert-remarkable-images-to-text` | Transcribes imported images and appends the text to the card. |

They cannot be edited or deleted, and project actions may not reuse their ids.

See also: [Placeholders](placeholders.md), [Running actions](running-actions.md), [Agent setup](agent-setup.md), [Cookbook](cookbook.md).

# Release process

mdÂ² tracks its own work with mdÂ². The mechanics below are the same ones any project gets.

## Cards during a release

Active cards live in the working folder. Each card is a feature (`F_`), job (`J_`), or bug (`B_`) and moves across the board as it is designed, implemented, and finished.

## Completing a release

**Complete release** (Run tab of the menu) asks for a release name and then:

1. creates a subfolder with that name under the releases folder;
2. moves every active card into it;
3. moves images referenced by those cards along with them, so relative links keep working;
4. leaves the board empty for the next cycle.

Release names must be plain (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`).

Cards you want off the board without belonging to a release go to the archived folder instead.

In this repository the result looks like [`design/releases/0_0_3/`](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/blob/main/design/releases/0_0_3/): one Markdown file per card plus `release_notes.md`.

## Release notes

`release_notes.md` in the release folder is written from the cards it contains â€” one user-visible line per change, not per commit. See [`design/releases/0_0_3/release_notes.md`](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/blob/main/design/releases/0_0_3/release_notes.md) for the tone.

## Versioning

`desktop/package.json` is authoritative for the product version; packaging reads it and names the artifacts after it. Bump it before building.

## Shipping a Windows build

```powershell
cd app && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test
cd ../desktop && npm run lint && npm run test
cd .. && npm run build:windows
```

The build fails on unsigned or unverifiable artifacts, missing packaged files, a dev-server URL leaking into the bundle, or stray certificate and source-map files. Smoke-test the installed build with the dev server stopped: open a local Git project, edit and commit a file, list branches, run an action, and install over the previous version to confirm settings survive.

Details and signing configuration: [`desktop/packaging/BUILDING_WINDOWS.md`](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/blob/main/desktop/packaging/BUILDING_WINDOWS.md).

See also: [Development setup](development-setup.md), [Project layout](../concepts/project-layout.md).

Read spec and traced action definitions, run execution, popup prompts, bridge, and release dialog. No edits made.

### Change plan and tasks

- [ ] **Block 1 — Action definitions:** Add optional `version` input request to shared types, validation, graph loading, editor select, and error routing. Test save, reload, both action types, and rejection of unknown values.
- [ ] **Block 2 — Run input:** Request version once before any linked action executes. Add run-ID response through Electron bridge and dialog. Settle wait on Cancel, window closure, run cancellation, and shutdown. Reject invalid, duplicate, and late responses. Fail unattended runs before execution when version is missing. Add focused tests.
- [ ] **Block 3 — Substitution:** Carry run value through commands, agent prompts, linked phases, and edited popup prompts. Make missing `{{version}}` fail clearly. Cover resolver callers and prompt preparation with tests.
- [ ] **Block 4 — Version script:** Add repository-specific script and action. Preflight files, write each file atomically, and test exact version updates and failures.
- [ ] **Block 5 — Release reuse:** Offer version from a successful run as editable release name. Keep existing release confirmation. Test retention and clearing.
- [ ] **Block 6 — Finish:** Update action docs; run related tests and app/desktop lint, not full suites. After implementation passes, set **specified external feature file** status to `ready`.

**Decisions for approval:** I propose strict `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` values, updating `app/package.json`, `desktop/package.json`, and their lockfiles’ root package versions. Root `package.json` has no version. I propose release suggestion lasts only within current app session and project; next successful version run replaces it, successful release clears it, and app restart clears it.

{
  "id": "21471796-1562-448a-b7cb-623599dabcea",
  "label": "prepare project",
  "description": "Makes certain that all projects are properly installed. ready for testing",
  "type": "agent",
  "appliesTo": {
    "kind": "project"
  },
  "phrases": [],
  "prompt": "Your task is to prepare this project for development.

Instructions:

1. Start by locating and reading the \`README.md\` file in the current directory.
2. Follow the setup instructions in that README exactly.
3. If the main README refers to additional \`README.md\` files in subdirectories, or if subdirectories contain setup instructions that are required for development, read those as well.
4. Perform all necessary project setup steps, including (where applicable):
   1. Installing dependencies.
   2. Installing toolchains or SDKs.
   3. Restoring packages.
   4. Creating generated files.
   5. Running bootstrap or setup scripts.
   6. Initializing git submodules.
   7. Installing workspace/package manager dependencies.
   8. Building any required generated artifacts.
5. Do not start long-running processes such as development servers or watch tasks unless the README explicitly requires them as part of setup.
6. If any step requires user input, elevated privileges, secrets, credentials, or external configuration, stop and explain exactly what is needed before proceeding.
7. If multiple package managers or setup methods are available, use the one recommended by the project's documentation.
8. If the documentation contains conflicting instructions, prefer the instructions in the top-level \`README.md\` and explain any conflict.
9. When setup is complete, provide a concise summary including:
   1. The steps that were performed.
   2. Any issues or warnings encountered.
   3. Any manual steps the developer still needs to complete.
   4. Whether the project appears ready for development.

Do not make assumptions beyond what is documented. Base your actions on the project's documentation whenever possible.
You do not need to run linting or tests after a fresh install.
Be brief, but never compress away the subject, timing, or causal chain. Define ambiguous technical phrases. use $caveman skill"
}

{
  "id": "update-project-version",
  "label": "Update project version",
  "description": "Generate and run a version update script for this project.",
  "type": "agent",
  "appliesTo": { "kind": "project" },
  "userInput": { "type": "version", "prompt": "Version for this project" },

I traced the current, uncommitted implementation. **Electron owns the run and the version value; React owns the editor, question dialog, and release-name suggestion.** The main gap is that the promised version update script has not been implemented.

### How a run works

1. **Definition and editing — shared code and React.** An action JSON file can declare `userInput: { "type": "version", "prompt": "…" }`. Shared validation accepts only `version`, rejects unknown fields, and carries the field into the resolved action graph. The React editor offers None or Version and an optional question; saving converts that choice back to JSON. See [validation](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/shared/action_definitions.mjs:229) and [editor fields](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/actions/editor/action_definition_fields.tsx:233).

2. **Start and gating — Electron.** `ActionRunnerService` walks the root action and linked `onBefore`, `on`, and `onAfter` actions. If any asks for a version, an interactive `ActionRun` publishes a run-scoped `inputRequest` and waits **before entering the action chain**. It asks once, even if several linked actions declare the field. An unattended start without an explicit version fails before a run is created; supplied versions are checked for non-whitespace text. See [request detection](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/action/action_runner_service.js:52), [start](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/action/action_runner_service.js:178), and [wait](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js:293).

3. **Question and answer — React through the Electron bridge.** The renderer registry puts `inputRequest` events into a pending-request service. The app-level dialog shows the oldest request, prefilled from project configuration. Confirm saves `project.lastVersion`, then calls `answerActionVersion(runId, version)` through the preload bridge. Electron validates again and resolves that run’s wait. Cancel calls `cancelActionRun`; Electron rejects the pending wait and finishes the run as cancelled. See [dialog](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/actions/run/action_version_dialog.tsx:12), [bridge dispatch](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.js:539), and [answer handling](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js:332).

4. **Execution and reuse — Electron.** The value lives on `ActionRun`, so command actions, agent actions, and linked phases receive the same value. The text resolvers replace `{{version}}`; encountering that placeholder without a value throws. Prompt preparation deliberately leaves `{{version}}` visible in an editable popup prompt, and Electron substitutes it when that prompt executes. See [command execution](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/action/action_command_executor.js:82), [agent execution](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/action/action_agent_executor.js:62), and [prompt preparation](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/action/action_runner_service.js:258).

5. **Release reuse — React and project persistence.** `lastVersion` is saved in project configuration and offered as an editable initial release name. Completing a release still requires the user’s confirmation. The value survives restart and is **never cleared after release**. See [suggestion](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/shell/menu/app_menu.tsx:491) and [release dialog](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/shell/project/complete_release_dialog.tsx:39).

### Architectural issues I found

- **The script requirement is unmet.** The new [template action](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/project_template/actions/update-project-version.json) tells an *agent* to inspect a project, create a script, and run it. There is no fixed project-specific script, agreed manifest list, or tested file-update operation. That makes the result dependent on an agent run and does not satisfy the design’s script acceptance criterion.

- **Free-form input is inserted into a shell command.** Validation requires only non-whitespace text, while the command executor substitutes it into a string launched with `shell: true` ([executor](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/action/action_command_executor.js:7)). A version containing shell syntax can change what a command action does. This needs an explicit decision about accepted version syntax or safe argument passing before treating command actions as safe.

- **Confirm writes and commits project config before Electron accepts the answer.** The dialog saves first ([dialog](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/actions/run/action_version_dialog.tsx:29)); desktop config persistence commits that change to Git ([persistence](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/project/project_files.js:375)). If the run was cancelled while the save was in progress, or the answer is rejected as late, the proposed release name can still change and be committed although no action ran. A config-save failure also prevents an otherwise valid answer from reaching the waiting run.

- **Recovery can leave a stale question visible.** The renderer removes a pending request on local confirmation or a terminal *event* ([registry](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/actions/action_run_registry.ts:796)). Its recovered-terminal-result path and `stop()` do not clear that separate request service. Replaying a request followed by later running events can likewise leave it displayed. Confirm would then be rejected as late; Cancel could target a run that has already advanced. This is a code-path finding, not a failure covered by the current tests.

- **Release reuse has no lifecycle beyond “most recent confirmed answer.”** It is project scoped, but an unrelated later version action can overwrite the suggestion, and completing a release leaves it in place. That behavior is documented; it still deserves a product decision because the dialog may propose an old release name.

The focused tests I ran passed: **93 desktop tests and 51 app tests**. They cover the normal request, cancellation, substitution, and dialog paths, but they do not establish safety for the shell input, config-save race, recovery cleanup, or a concrete version script. I made no file changes.

entries.content:
1. **It uses the commit batcher.** React stages the `userInput` choice in the action draft. On the editor’s commit boundary, `ActionService` serializes the definition to JSON and `DataService` queues the action file in `CommitBatcher`. It is not a direct file save from the component. [Editor](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/actions/editor/action_definition_fields.tsx:65) · [persistence path](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/data/data_service.ts:289)

2. **It checks specifically for `userInput.type === 'version'`.** Merely having `userInput` defined does not trigger a generic request. `version` is currently the only valid type. A caller can supply `runInput.version`; then Electron uses it without showing the dialog. [Detection](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/action/action_runner_service.js:52)

3. You’re right about the other points. The agent action that generates a project-specific script is intentional. Free-form command input is intentional here. Saving the last entered value even if the run is later cancelled is desirable. Keeping that value as the release suggestion needs no further lifecycle.

4. **The dialog behavior was wrong, and I changed it.** Previously Confirm waited for config persistence and Electron’s response before closing. It now closes immediately on Confirm or Cancel. Persistence and submission continue afterward; a persistence failure is reported but does not strand the run without its answer. I also clear stale requests when execution advances, recovery reports a finished run, or the registry stops. [Dialog](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/actions/run/action_version_dialog.tsx:16) · [request cleanup](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/actions/action_run_registry.ts:795)

The focused app tests pass (**52 tests**), and app lint passes.
